assessmentSummary.identity: A no-flight bilateral action that moves rapidly from tall posture into a declared athletic stance and holds a static no-rebound finish.
currentCardFindings: Three redundant definitions describe the same rapid bilateral descent and stick and are consolidated into this survivor.
The legacy survivor text incorrectly described a box jump; the corrected card explicitly excludes flight, rebound, and external height.
Four media links have current public oEmbed metadata only and remain unviewed candidates.

currentCardSnapshot.description: Stand tall with feet at the declared width and arms in the declared start position. Rapidly drive the arms down while lowering the center of mass into a bilateral athletic stance; contact or settle through the whole foot, align each knee with the foot, organize the trunk over the pelvis, and hold the finish for the declared time without a rebound or extra step. Reset fully and stop before speed, contact sound, alignment, breathing, or control changes.

population.medicalScope: This card does not diagnose, rehabilitate, or clear an athlete; follow the care plan and local scope.

claims: Privacy-enhanced YouTube embed URLs can be constructed with youtube-nocookie.com.

The candidate watch URLs returned public oEmbed metadata on 2026-07-26; embed playback, full-video exact matching, cue and safety quality, captions, accessibility, reviewer identity, and approval remain unresolved.

evidence.sourceTitle: Training interventions to reduce the risk of injury to the lower extremity joints during landing movements in adult athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
claims: A rapid tall-to-athletic bilateral descent followed by a static no-rebound finish defines this card; no flight or external height is required.
Athletic, landing, and control labels name the same action, while stance, arm start, depth, speed, and hold time are variant or dose dimensions.

evidence.sourceTitle: Training interventions to reduce the risk of injury to the lower extremity joints during landing movements in adult athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
claims: The card is a bilateral land-and-squat preparation pattern without a required aerial phase.
Jump, rebound, unilateral, box, depth-drop, and moving-entry tasks remain separate definitions.

evidence.sourceTitle: Training interventions to reduce the risk of injury to the lower extremity joints during landing movements in adult athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
claims: Rapid ankle, knee, and hip flexion control organizes the descent while foot, frontal-plane, transverse-plane, and trunk control stabilize the finish.
The listed muscles describe contributing roles and do not claim isolation or exact activation magnitude.

evidence.sourceTitle: The Use of Augmented Information for Reducing Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury Risk During Jump Landings: A Systematic Review
claims: Landing instruction and feedback can alter measured landing mechanics, but direct transfer to this exact no-flight snap-down has not been established.
The quality contract therefore records whole-foot pressure, knee-foot alignment, trunk control, contact sound, and a motionless finish without claiming injury prevention.

evidence.sourceTitle: The Use of Augmented Information for Reducing Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury Risk During Jump Landings: A Systematic Review
claims: Exercise complexity rises with faster descent, more demanding arm starts, deeper target positions, stricter alignment, and longer stick criteria; physical difficulty remains modest without flight or external load.
Overall exercise difficulty equals the greater of complexity and physical difficulty; athlete proficiency is not an exercise-card field.

evidence.sourceTitle: Training interventions to reduce the risk of injury to the lower extremity joints during landing movements in adult athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
claims: Load is bodyweight through a bilateral closed chain with rapid eccentric control and a low contact budget.
Dose stays quality-limited and ends before descent speed, contact sound, alignment, breathing, or finish control changes.

evidence.sourceTitle: Training interventions to reduce the risk of injury to the lower extremity joints during landing movements in adult athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
claims: Use a flat dry nonslip floor, overhead clearance, a marked personal station, and direct observation.
Do not add a box, drop height, rebound, or conditioning density to this identity.

evidence.sourceTitle: The Use of Augmented Information for Reducing Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury Risk During Jump Landings: A Systematic Review
claims: Use short sets of fully reset repetitions with a declared two-to-three-second stick and ample rest.
Exact repetitions and scores are programming proposals pending calibration rather than externally validated prescriptions.

evidence.sourceTitle: The Use of Augmented Information for Reducing Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury Risk During Jump Landings: A Systematic Review
claims: Declare stance, arm start, target depth, repetitions, hold time, quality gate, and stop signal before starting.
Reach tall, snap down, organize the whole foot and knee, freeze without rebound, breathe, and reset.

evidence.sourceTitle: Training interventions to reduce the risk of injury to the lower extremity joints during landing movements in adult athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
claims: Stop for symptoms, giving way, uncontrolled contact, repeated knee or trunk collapse, extra steps, breath holding, fear, or unsafe floor conditions.
A failed stick is recorded rather than hidden or converted into another repetition.

evidence.sourceTitle: Training interventions to reduce the risk of injury to the lower extremity joints during landing movements in adult athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
claims: Use as low-impact landing-shape preparation before more demanding jump, sprint, or deceleration work when it improves the session task.
Do not use completion of this drill alone as proof of readiness for high-impact activity.

evidence.sourceTitle: The Use of Augmented Information for Reducing Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury Risk During Jump Landings: A Systematic Review
claims: Athlete support names expected effort, unexpected symptoms, self-checks, access options, and nonvideo instruction.
The athlete reports symptoms, fear, loss of pressure, or a failed stick immediately.

evidence.sourceTitle: The Use of Augmented Information for Reducing Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury Risk During Jump Landings: A Systematic Review
claims: Coach support covers front and side observation, fault correction order, demonstration, group spacing, and exact recording.
The coach reduces speed before increasing depth or volume and stops for persistent faults or symptoms.

evidence.sourceTitle: The Use of Augmented Information for Reducing Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury Risk During Jump Landings: A Systematic Review
claims: A slower drop, shallower depth, hands-at-chest start, visual floor marker, fewer repetitions, or longer reset can improve access.
A slow Drop Squat to Stick is a separate regression identity rather than silently changing the rapid snap-down contract.

evidence.sourceTitle: Training interventions to reduce the risk of injury to the lower extremity joints during landing movements in adult athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
claims: Arm position and depth are modifiers; athletic, landing, and control names are the same identity.
Slow drop squats, jumps, rebounds, unilateral finishes, and external-height tasks require separate definitions.

alternateAssessments.name: Snap-Down to Athletic Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: Athletic names the canonical bilateral finish and adds no action.

alternateAssessments.name: Snapdown Landing Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: Landing stick names the defining terminal hold.

alternateAssessments.name: Snap-Down to Stick Control Version
alternateAssessments.rationale: Control is the canonical no-rebound delivery intent.

alternateAssessments.name: Arms-at-Chest Snap-Down
alternateAssessments.rationale: Arm start changes cueing and momentum but preserves the rapid descent and stick.

alternateAssessments.name: Shallow Snap-Down to Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: A shallower owned finish changes range and dose without adding an action.

alternateAssessments.name: Drop Squat to Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: A deliberately slower descent removes the defining rapid snap.

alternateAssessments.name: Snap-Down to Jump and Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: A takeoff and aerial phase add a jump after the snap-down.

alternateAssessments.name: Snap-Down to Pogo Rebound
alternateAssessments.rationale: A rebound replaces the static no-rebound finish.

alternateAssessments.name: Single-Leg Snap-Down Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: A unilateral finish changes laterality, balance, load distribution, and consequence.

alternateAssessments.name: Box or Depth Snap-Down Stick
alternateAssessments.rationale: External height adds flight or drop-height exposure absent from this card.
